purpose.description: Construct nonlinear counterexamples demonstrating failure of target identifiability when linear rank conditions are insufficient.
purpose.role: Extend interface failure analysis from linear null-space arguments to nonlinear observational equivalence classes.
not_used_for: proving all nonlinear targets are unidentifiable
replacing nonlinear factorization analysis with linear rank tests

system_class.description: Declared nonlinear system family with nonlinear target functional.

observation_operator.description: Behavioral interface mapping nonlinear systems to observed trajectories.

target_functional.description: Nonlinear future target evaluated over system dynamics.

counterexamples.description: Two nonlinear systems agree on all observed interface trajectories but diverge on the nonlinear target.
Systems share identical local response but differ under nonlinear continuation.
Different nonlinear evolution laws intersect at observed times but produce different held-out futures.

linear_rank_condition.reason: No fixed linear row-space representation of the target exists over the full class.

theorem_connection.failure_reason: Observation equivalence classes contain multiple target values.
theorem_connection.result: No factorization exists for the declared interface over the nonlinear class.

proven: declared nonlinear class contains interface-induced ambiguities

decision.meaning: The tested nonlinear interface does not preserve all target-relevant distinctions.

notes: Gate 006 separates nonlinear identifiability from linear rank sufficiency.
A zero local Jacobian obstruction does not imply global impossibility.
The central criterion remains factorization through the observation operator.
